Thanks for the note, Yuki — really helpful context. Looping Ava (solutions engineer) and Vivek (CS lead) to make sure we don't hit any client calendar quirks during the invite flow.

Short explanation: when an invite is authored strictly in UTC and marked without an explicit TZ ID in the DTSTART property, some clients treat it as a "floating" time or interpret it differently (Exchange/Outlook historically has odd behavior for ICS files created by certain APIs). That can push the visible local date forward for zones east of UTC — which is exactly what you're seeing.

Action: I've recreated the calendar event with explicit TZ IDs (Asia/Tokyo, Asia/Singapore, Australia/Sydney) in the ICS and moved the start away from the midnight boundary. Proposed new single slot: 09:30 JST / 08:30 SGT / 11:30 AEST on Tue, 10 Aug.

I've attached the updated agenda and re-sent the invite (link below). If your Sydney colleagues still see a date mismatch, please have them check whether their Outlook desktop has an Exchange caching issue — accepting the invite from web/OWA usually shows the correct local date.

New calendar link: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=abc123-redwood-midori (updated)
Attachment: Redwood-demo-agenda.pdf
